question.text: Let $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation: The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{a} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2\cdot(-5)+(-2)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 1}{2^2 +(-2)^2 +2^2 +2^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-10-2-6+2}{4+4+4+4}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-16}{16}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= -\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= -1\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{a} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2 \cdot 3 + 0 \cdot 2 + (-2) \cdot (-3) + 2 \cdot 3}{2^2+0^2+(-2)^2+2^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6+0+6+6}{4+0+4+4}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{18}{12}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{a} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 2 + 0 \cdot (-1) + 1 \cdot 5} {1^2+1^2+0^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2+2+0+5}{1+1+0+1}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{3}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 3\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 3\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{a} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 4}{4^2+2^2+(-3)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\ &= \dfrac{4+4+9+4}{16+4+9+1}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{21}{30}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7}{10}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7}{10}\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{14}{5} \\ \dfrac{7}{5} \\ -\dfrac{21}{10} \\ \dfrac{7}{10} \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{a}\}.$
question.explanation:
The vector projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}\}$ is given by

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\,\mathbf{b} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}} \mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 4 + (-2) \cdot (-4) + 6 \cdot 2}{6^2+2^2+(-2)^2+6^2}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{12+8+8+12}{36+4+4+36}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{40}{80}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Distance  Between a Vector and a One-Dimensional Subspace

question.text: Let $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation:
The distance between the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the vector space $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by $\| \mathbf{x} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}} \|$, where ${\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}}$ in the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$ \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2\cdot 4+4\cdot 5+0\cdot 1+2\cdot 4}{2^2 +4^2 +0^2 +2^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8+20+0+8}{4+16+0+4}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \begin{align*} \| \mathbf{x} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}} \| &= \sqrt{(x_1-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_1)^2+(x_2-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_2)^2+(x_3-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_3)^2+(x_4-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_4)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{(4-3)^2+(5-6)^2+(1-0)^2+(4-3)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{1+1+1+1} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{4} \\[3pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}\}\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}} \mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6\cdot 5+3\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-1)+6\cdot 4}{6^2 +3^2 +(-3)^2 +6^2}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{30+3+3+24}{36+9+9+36}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{60}{90}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{3}\mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we get the following:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{y} & = \text{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\,\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \mathbf{z} & = \mathbf{x} - \text{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\,\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Notice that $\mathbf{y} \in \text{Span}\{\mathbf{a}\}$ and $\mathbf{z} \perp \text{Span}\{\mathbf{a}\},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $\mathbf{z} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}.$

question.text: Let $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
question.explanation:
The distance between the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the vector space $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by $\| \mathbf{x} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}} \|$, where ${\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}}$ in the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1 \cdot 4 + 2 \cdot 4 + (-2) \cdot (-2) + 1 \cdot 4}{1^2+2^2+(-2)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4+8+4+4}{1+4+4+1}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20}{10}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \begin{align*} \| \mathbf{x} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{x}}} \| &= \sqrt{(x_1-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_1)^2+(x_2-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_2)^2+(x_3-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_3)^2+(x_4-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{x}}}_4)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{(4-2)^2+(4-4)^2+(-2-(-4))^2+(4-2)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{4+0+4+4} \\[3pt] &= 2\sqrt{3}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{u} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the distance between $\mathbf{u}$ and $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}.$
question.explanation:
The distance between the vector $\mathbf{u}$ and the vector space $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}$ is given by $\| \mathbf{u} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{u}}} \|$, where ${\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{u}}}$ in the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{u}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{u}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}.$

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{w}}\,\mathbf{u} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{u}}{\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{w}} \mathbf{w} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2 \cdot 4 + 1 \cdot 2 + (-2) \cdot (-2) + 1 \cdot 6}{2^2+1^2+(-2)^2+1^2}\mathbf{w} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8+2+4+6}{4+1+4+1}\mathbf{w} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20}{10}\mathbf{w} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{w} \\[5pt] &= 2\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{u}}}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \begin{align*} \| \mathbf{u} - {\Large\hat{\normalsize\mathbf{u}}} \| &= \sqrt{(u_1-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{u}}}_1)^2+(u_2-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{u}}}_2)^2+(u_3-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{u}}}_3)^2+(u_4-{\Large\hat{\normalsize{u}}}_4)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{(4-4)^2+(2-2)^2+(-2-(-4))^2+(6-2)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{0+0+4+16} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{20} \\[3pt] &= 2\sqrt{5}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector onto the Solution Space of a System of Equations

question.text: Given the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system. \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -10 \\ -13 \\1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \begin{cases} x_1 - x_2- 3x_3= 0 \\ 2x_1-x_2+x_3=0\end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} M &= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get $x_2=-7x_3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1-(-7x_3)-3x_3= 0 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=-4x_3. \]

So, the general solution is \[ \begin{bmatrix} -4x_3 \\ -7x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = x_3 \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -7 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_3 \in\mathbb{R}.\]

Consequently, $\mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -7 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\right\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system:

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(-10) \cdot (-4)+ (-13) \cdot (-7) + 1 \cdot (1)} {(-4)^2+(-7)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{132}{66}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -7 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ -14 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

question.text: Given the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system. \[ \mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2=0 \\ 3x_1+9x_2=0 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} M &= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 9 & 0 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + (-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get $x_1=-3x_2.$ So, the general solution is \[ \begin{bmatrix} -3x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} =x_2\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Consequently, $\mathcal{B}=\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system: \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(-4) \cdot (-3) + 8 \cdot 1}{\left(-3\right)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20}{10}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -6 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

question.text: Given the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system. \[ \mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \begin{cases} 2x_1-x_2=0 \\ -x_1+\dfrac12x_2=0 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} M &= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & \dfrac12 & 0 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + \dfrac12R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get $x_1=\dfrac12x_2.$ So, the general solution is \[ \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac12x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} =x_2\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac12 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Consequently, $\mathcal{B}=\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac12 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system: \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4 \cdot \dfrac12 + 3 \cdot 1}{\left(\dfrac12\right)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{\dfrac14+1}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 4\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 4\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac12 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\4 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

question.text: Given the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system. \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -5 \\4 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \begin{cases} x_1 - x_3 = 0 \\ 2x_1+x_2+x_3=0\end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} M &= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. Now, from the first equation, we get $x_1=x_3$ and from the second equation $x_2=-3x_3.$

So, the general solution is \[ \begin{bmatrix} x_3 \\ -3x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = x_3 \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_3 \in\mathbb{R}.\]

Consequently, $\mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\right\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system:

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3 \cdot 1+ (-5) \cdot (-3) + 4\cdot 1}{1^2+(-3)^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{22}{11}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &=2\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\-3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2\\ -6 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

question.text: Given the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system. \[ \mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \begin{cases} x_1-2x_2=0 \\ 2x_1-4x_2=0 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} M &= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get $x_1=-2x_2.$ So, the general solution is \[ \begin{bmatrix} 2x_2 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} =x_2\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Consequently, $\mathcal{B}=\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the solution space of the system: \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{x} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 1}{2^2+1^2}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10}{5}\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= 2\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
